## Objective
Make health reads fail closed: unreadable inputs surface as WARN/unknown, never PASS. Today telemetry.iter_jsonl swallows OSError so pi-bridge/retrieval checks report 'no recent failures', and an index-staleness OSError resolves to stale=False.

## Design summary
Convention is pre-decided: an unreadable input produces WARN with the underlying error in the check detail; it never produces PASS and never crashes the whole health run. Defect sites: memento/telemetry.py:162 (iter_jsonl swallows OSError); memento/health.py:1432, :1583, :702, :1458 (checks that PASS on the swallowed error / staleness OSError to stale=False). Note: line numbers are from the 2026-07-02 audit against main; if mem-124 has already landed on your branch, locate the same logic by content, not line number.

## File scope
Include: memento/telemetry.py, memento/health.py, new/updated tests under tests/.
Exclude: queue health (mem-124), timezone handling (mem-126), everything else.

## Constraints
No git push or PR creation - local branch/diff only. Use .venv/bin/python for every command. Work test-first: for each of the four cited sites, a failing test that makes the input unreadable (chmod 000 or missing file) and asserts non-PASS, then the fix. If ambiguous, pause and ask.

## Verification
From the repo root:
1. .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/ (new unreadable-input tests green; suite green)
2. .venv/bin/python -m ruff check .
3. .venv/bin/python -m ruff format --check .
4. .venv/bin/python -m compileall -q memento hooks scripts
dependencies: Ordering: runs after mem-124-queue-health-check (both edit health.py; workspace serialization, not semantic)
